questions.answer: $\dfrac{dy}{dx}=2x$. At $x=1$: tangent gradient $=2$, so normal gradient $=-\dfrac{1}{2}$. Normal: $y-1=-\dfrac{1}{2}(x-1)$, so $y=-\dfrac{1}{2}x+\dfrac{3}{2}$.

Find the coordinates of the stationary point of $y=x^2-6x+11$, and determine whether it is a maximum or minimum.
questions.answer: $\dfrac{dy}{dx}=2x-6=0$, so $x=3$. $y=9-18+11=2$. Stationary point: $(3,2)$. Since $\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2}=2>0$, it is a minimum.

sections.heading: A well-designed word problem: minimizing material for a can

questions.q: This question has two parts. A cylindrical can must have a volume of $500\pi$ cm$^3$. Let $r$ be the radius and $h$ the height. (a) Show that the surface area is $S=2\pi r^2+\dfrac{1000\pi}{r}$. (b) Find the radius that minimizes the surface area, and confirm it is a minimum using the second derivative.
questions.answer: (a) Volume: $\pi r^2h=500\pi$, so $h=\dfrac{500}{r^2}$. Surface area (two circular ends plus the curved side): $S=2\pi r^2+2\pi rh=2\pi r^2+2\pi r\left(\dfrac{500}{r^2}\right)=2\pi r^2+\dfrac{1000\pi}{r}$. (b) $\dfrac{dS}{dr}=4\pi r-\dfrac{1000\pi}{r^2}=0$, so $4\pi r=\dfrac{1000\pi}{r^2}$, giving $r^3=250$, so $r=\sqrt[3]{250}\approx6.30$ cm. Second derivative: $\dfrac{d^2S}{dr^2}=4\pi+\dfrac{2000\pi}{r^3}$, which is always positive for $r>0$, confirming this is a minimum.
